text: Assistant: Found it. The global `mouseup` listener has no guard against firing when the mouseup itself lands on the toolbar button — so clicking "Highlight" makes the listener destroy-and-recreate the toolbar mid-click, and the browser then never dispatches the `click` event to the now-detached original button (a well-known DOM quirk: removing an element between mousedown/mouseup suppresses the synthesized click). That's why nothing happens at all. [...] Assistant: **Fixed and verified.** The bug you hit — clicking "Highlight" doing nothing, not even prompting a signature — was a real DOM race: the global `mouseup` listener that opens the toolbar wasn't ignoring mouseup events that landed on the toolbar itself, so clicking it destroyed-and-recreated the button mid-click, which silently suppresses the browser's `click` event on the now-detached original element. Added a guard (`f7z.io/src/highlights.js`) so the listener ignores mouseup events originating inside `.n-hl-toolbar`, rebuilt `js/highlights.js`, and re-ran the full flow in a real browser with a fake NIP-07 provider: sign-in → select text → click Highlight → `<mark class="n-highlight">` appears wrapping the selection → hover tooltip shows the highlighter's name/npub and timestamp. All confirmed working.
